newsitem.title: USA: NiGas extends "critical day" through Fri.
newsitem.headline: NiGas extends "critical day" through Fri.

text.p: Northern Illinois Gas Co said Wednesday it has declared another "critical day" for Friday as expected, limiting gas deliveries from Illinois pipelines and storage facilities.
Withdrawal limits, which are now in place for both Thursday and Friday, were as a result of severe cold in the Midwest.
Temperatures are forecast to dip to 15-25 degrees Fahrenheit below normal beginning late Thursday.
A critical day affects deliveries for the day beginning at noon (1200 CST), in this case both Thursday and Friday.
It can be declared from November 1 to April 1 when storage withdrawals and supplies from NiGas' seven storage facilities at times need to be limited to meet contractual obligations.
As a result of the critical days, spot prices at the Chicago city-gate soared to a high of $6.50 per million British thermal units, up at least $2 from Tuesday.
Peoples Energy Co also declared a critical day for Thursday because of the cold.
